A_target.statement:
Let $\LL$ be a [[Definition:Countable Set|countable]] first-order language, $\MM$ an $\LL$-[[Definition:Structure (Model Theory)|structure]] and $X \subseteq M$ countable.
Then $\MM$ has a countable [[Definition:Elementary Substructure|elementary substructure]] $\NN$ with $X \subseteq N$.

B_source.statement:
Let $N \subseteq M$.
Then $N$ is the universe of an elementary substructure of $\MM$ {{iff}} for every formula $\map \phi {x, \bar y}$ and $\bar b \in N$, if $\MM \models \exists x \, \map \phi {x, \bar b}$ then $\MM \models \map \phi {a, \bar b}$ for some $a \in N$.
This is the [[Tarski-Vaught Test]].

object_map.reformulation: Close X under countably many Skolem functions in countably many stages, so that the Tarski-Vaught condition holds by construction.

validity_conditions: The Axiom of Choice is used to choose the Skolem functions.
Countability of the language bounds the number of formulas, keeping every stage countable.
proof_plan: For each formula $\exists x \, \map \phi {x, \bar y}$, choose a [[Definition:Skolem Function|Skolem function]] $f_\phi$ with $\MM \models \map \phi {\map {f_\phi} {\bar b}, \bar b}$ whenever $\MM \models \exists x \, \map \phi {x, \bar b}$.

Let $N_0 = X$ together with the interpretations of the constants, plus one point if this is empty.
Let $N_{k + 1}$ add to $N_k$ all values $\map {f_\phi} {\bar b}$ and all values of function symbols at tuples from $N_k$, and let $N = \bigcup_k N_k$.
There are countably many formulas and finite tuples from a countable set, so each $N_k$ is countable, and so is $N$.
